column1: Rovem — Component, Mission and Progression Values (Proposal)
All input values are proposals, set by reasoning and simulation, to be confirmed in playtesting.
Legend
Blue text on yellow = proposed input. Change these to rebalance; formulas update.
Black text = formula. Green fill = passes, red fill = fails.
Sheets
Inputs: constants, parts, surfaces, mission parameters and power-ups.
Builds: every chassis × wheels × motor combination, calculated with the Physics Model Specification formulas.

Simulation: results of the step-by-step simulation in the Physics Model Specification (1/120 s steps; throttle and brake levels read at the end of each step; finish time is the end of the step that reaches the line), used to set the mission limits.
Pass check: which builds pass each mission, using the simulation results and the mission limits.
Progression: Knowledge earned and spent.
Spread: lowest and highest value of each result, to check that part choices matter.
Formulas used (Physics Model Specification)
m = chassis + wheels + motor mass;  R = mg;  rolling friction F_r = μ_r × k_r × R;  grip limit F_lim = μ_g × k_g × R
Max acceleration a = (min(F_d,max, F_lim) − F_r) / m;  max braking deceleration = (min(F_b,max, F_lim) + F_r) / m
Mission 1: if top speed is reached first, t = v_max / a + (S − v_max² / 2a) / v_max; otherwise t = √(2S / a)
Mission 2: ice time t = √(2L / a_ice); coasting distance on sand S = v² / (2 μ_r k_r g) with v² = 2 a_ice L, so mass and motor cancel
Mission 3: brake force builds up linearly over T_b (capped by grip), then stays at full; distance = build-up distance + v² / 2a
Notes
Builds sheet Mission 1 and 2 times ignore the throttle build-up; the Simulation sheet includes it (about 0.1–0.5 s more).
g = 9.8 m/s² as in the textbook. Question numericals state g = 10 m/s².
One rover model in the MVP, so one maximum brake force for every build.
Spread counts the faster Mission 1 route from the Simulation sheet (17 of 27 builds), as the SRS states. Builds column U uses the closed-form times, which ignore throttle build-up, and shows 18.
Mission 3 is on asphalt. The rover is towed at 15 m/s and released at the first brake input after the brake line; stopping distance is measured from that input.
Mission 2 coasting distance is measured from the rover's position at the end of the step that reaches the power-cut line.
